security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel KVM code running in HS-mode reads senvcfg.SSE to determine whether shadow stacks are active for guest U/VU-mode while henvcfg.SSE=0. Under the clarified spec, senvcfg.SSE reads as 0 in this state but the underlying value is preserved—it is not cleared. If the kernel caches this zero read, or makes a security-sensitive decision (e.g., skipping shadow stack page-table setup, skipping ssp save/restore, or reporting SSE=0 to the guest) without accounting for the fact that the underlying SSE bit may be 1 and will take effect as soon as henvcfg.SSE transitions to 1, the kernel's internal SSE tracking diverges from hardware state.
security_spec.summary: henvcfg.SSE=0 makes senvcfg.SSE read-as-zero without clearing the underlying bit; kernel KVM code reading senvcfg.SSE to track guest SSE state may operate on a stale view, causing shadow stack state corruption when henvcfg.SSE is later set to 1

findings.finding: henvcfg.SSE is never set in cfg->henvcfg even when Zicfiss is available to the guest. All other envcfg features (SVPBMT→PBMTE, SSTC→STCE, ZICBOM→CBIE|CBCFE, ZICBOZ→CBZE, SVADU→ADUE) are configured but SSE is omitted. Since henvcfg.SSE defaults to 0, guest VS-mode xSSE is always 0, making Zicfiss instructions trap regardless of what the VMM writes to senvcfg.SSE via ONE_REG.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Zicfiss extension adds the SSE field in henvcfg. If the SSE field is set to 1, the Zicfiss extension is activated in VS-mode. When the SSE field is 0, the Zicfiss extension remains inactive in VS-mode, and the following rules apply when V=1: ... The senvcfg.SSE field will read as zero and is read-only.

findings.finding: SBI_FWFT_SHADOW_STACK is listed in kvm_fwft_defined_features[] (line 69) so it is recognized as a defined feature, but it has NO entry in the features[] table. Only MISALIGNED_EXC_DELEG and POINTER_MASKING_PMLEN have set/get/reset callbacks. Consequently, kvm_fwft_get_feature() returns SBI_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED for shadow stack. A guest SBI FWFT_SET(SHADOW_STACK) call can never enable shadow stacks because the feature has no implementation. This means the guest VS-mode can never get henvcfg.SSE=1 via the SBI path either.

csr_swap(CSR_SENVCFG, csr->senvcfg) runs in HS-mode (V=0) before the V=1 guest entry. In HS-mode, senvcfg.SSE is fully writable and readable regardless of henvcfg.SSE — the read-as-zero masking applies only when V=1 per the spec. The guest senvcfg value (potentially with SSE=1 from VMM ONE_REG) is correctly written to hardware where it is preserved across the V=1 guest run. The csr_swap is followed by __kvm_riscv_switch_to() which executes sret to V=1.

findings.finding: After V=1 guest exit, csr_swap(CSR_SENVCFG, host_senvcfg) at line 770 reads back the hardware SENVCFG register in HS-mode (V=0). In HS-mode the SSE bit is fully readable — the underlying value preserved during the V=1 execution is returned intact. This correctly updates csr->senvcfg with the full value. The host envcfg is then restored. No stale-zero-cache problem exists because the read occurs in HS-mode, not VS-mode.

findings.finding: ONE_REG read of KVM_REG_RISCV_CSR_REG(senvcfg) returns csr->senvcfg from the software cache, which was last populated by csr_swap at exit time (line 770, V=0 context). The returned value correctly reflects the preserved SSE bit because the read-back occurred in HS-mode where the SSE bit is not masked. VMM sees the correct SSE state.

Host context switch writes next->thread.envcfg to CSR_ENVCFG (which is CSR_SENVCFG in S-mode). When shadow stack is enabled for the next task, thread.envcfg includes ENVCFG_SSE (set by set_shstk_status in usercfi.c:70). This correctly propagates SSE across host task switches.

findings.finding: Host userspace shadow stack management properly sets ENVCFG_SSE in task->thread.envcfg and writes CSR_ENVCFG. The envcfg_update_bits helper from switch_to.h:73-82 writes directly to hardware when task==current, which is the case here since prctl comes from the calling task. Host-side SSE handling is correct.
